$comment: Scene manifest — which of wafflebase's routes are editable in the design editor.
COMMITTED ON PURPOSE, and not a glob over app/**. Which routes are worth editing,
what each needs mocked, and which fixture makes it look real are curation decisions
that belong in a reviewable file. A glob would drag ~200 files through the TS
compiler on every metadata refresh and would silently add scenes that cannot mount.
This is population C: the manifest is wafflebase's, and `@wafflebase/design-editor`
reads it through `options.scenes` without knowing anything in it. Its schema is
`SceneConfig` in that package's `src/plugin/scenes.ts`, which is also where each
field's reasoning lives — `routePattern`, `shell`, `deferred` and the rest are
documented there rather than duplicated here.
`components` feeds the per-component CVA/token panels. `scenes` feeds the layout
editor. `mocks` names the providers a scene needs; `kind` picks the DOM or Canvas
adapter.
`shell: "app"` mounts the scene inside the REAL app/Layout.tsx (sidebar + header +
<Outlet/>), because that is how App.tsx renders it. Every route except /login is an
<Outlet/> body: rendered bare it is a padded box in an empty viewport, and judgements
about width, gutters and the header relationship are then made against the wrong
container. Shell scenes need `router`, `query`, `auth` and `tooltip` — the shell
itself fetches /workspaces, /analytics/enabled and /auth/me.
`documents` / `datasources` / `analytics` / `settings` point at the workspace-scoped
pages under app/workspaces/ — what Layout.tsx's sidebar actually links to
(`/w/:workspaceId/...`) once a workspace exists, which is the case for every real
user. The flat `/documents` / `/datasources` pages are Layout's no-workspace fallback
only, not the primary render path, so they are deliberately not manifest scenes.
`settings-personal` is a genuinely different page (appearance/theme), not a stale
duplicate of `settings` (workspace membership/API keys). Route params use the literal
`ws-fixture` id so `useParams()` resolves to exactly what the workspace fixtures are
keyed under.
EVERY SCENE IS `deferred` IN THIS PR, and each says why below. `deferred` keeps the
entry and its reasoning while generating no loader, which is exactly the state the
editor is in: PR 8c ships the token pipeline, and the scene runtime that mounts these
— the frame entry, SceneHost, providers.tsx, the fixtures and the offline Yorkie shim
— is PRs 10-12. A loader whose target cannot mount is not free even if never clicked:
the specifier is statically analysable, so Vite's dependency scanner crawls it at
startup. The flags come off in the PR that supplies what each scene is waiting for.
DOM scenes wait on `providers.tsx` alone. Rendered with no providers they are a bare
component with no router, and every param-gated query in them silently disables
itself.
CANVAS scenes additionally wait on the offline Yorkie provider. They mount the REAL
Sheets/Docs/Slides/Notes engines against a Document that is real but DETACHED — never
attached to a live Yorkie connection — which needs a dev-server-wide redirect of every
`@yorkie-js/react` import to a shim, plus seed content per docKey. `sheet-editor`
points at `document-detail.tsx` (the page that owns the `DocumentProvider`), not
`sheet-view.tsx` (a child that needs one from its parent and a `tabId` prop neither
this manifest nor a bare mount can supply).
`pdf-viewer` is deferred for a second, permanent reason: a binary PDF fixture, the
pdf.js worker and the `cmaps`/`standard_fonts` middleware are real weight for a scene
that exercises almost no design-system surface. It stays deferred after PRs 10-12.
